meta.random: numpy.random.default_rng(seed); province seed 0 for the figures, seeds 0-199 for the repeated runs
meta.weights: edge attribute 'weight' = cost divided by its median over the complete graph (no ranking changes); 'distance' = real Euclidean length (unit square, or km for Quebec) used for every length and detour measure
meta.tsp: networkx.approximation.traveling_salesman_problem with its default method (Christofides) on the complete graph, as in class. It is an approximation: the 1.5 guarantee needs the triangle inequality, which holds for (a) and generally fails for (b)-(e). The function first replaces each pair by its cheapest path, so for (b)-(e) the returned cycle can pass through a hub several times; 'tsp.repeated_visits' counts those repeats and the edges of such a closed walk are still added.
meta.stages: mst = minimum spanning tree on the cost; network = MST plus the TSP-cycle edges not already built
meta.detour: mean over all unordered town pairs of (shortest path over built roads on 'distance') / (straight line)
meta.top5_bottom5: 5 largest / 5 smallest populations, ties broken by town index

part1.choice_of_p: numpy Generator.geometric(p) returns k = 1, 2, 3, ... with mean 1/p, median about ln2/p and an exponentially thin tail. p = 0.1 gives a mean of 10 units; one unit is read as 1000 inhabitants, so the mean town has 10 000, the smallest possible has 1000 and the largest of 30 is typically near 35 000. The scale only multiplies all populations by one constant, which changes no MST or TSP result for any of the five costs and none of the ratios below.
part1.marker_area_formula: area(points^2) = 25 + 475 * (log10(pop) - log10(pop_min)) / (log10(pop_max) - log10(pop_min)); area is linear in log10(population) and spans 25 (smallest town of the figure) to 500 (largest); the legend prints three reference populations.

theory_geometric.tail: P(X > x) = (1-p)^x, exponential decay: constant mean excess, excess kurtosis ~ 6, no power-law tail

geometric_comparison.caveat: The real set is the 40 largest municipalities, so its median is far above the median municipality of the province; its largest/median ratio and top-5 share therefore understate the skew of the whole province. The geometric draws are compared at n = 40 on purpose.

part3_real_quebec.selection_rule: among cost variants (b)-(e) whose MST raises the mean degree of the 5 biggest towns above variant (a), the smallest total real MST length
part3_real_quebec.note_on_real_roads: The comparison with the Autoroute 20 / Autoroute 40 corridors is a comparison with the reader's knowledge: no road-network data was retrieved or used here.
